//routing: so each static content page has exactly ONE canonical URL. It also 308s
/index.html -> /, closing a duplicate of the homepage.
Do NOT add a catch-all SPA rewrite ( /(.*) -> /index.html ). The app has no
client-side router — multiplayer deep links are query strings, which never
need a rewrite — and a catch-all would silently serve the SPA shell at every
content URL, which Google reads as 11 duplicate homepages.

//: connect-src is an ALLOWLIST, not 'https:'. It previously permitted any
HTTPS/WSS host, which meant an XSS or a compromised dependency could
exfiltrate to anywhere. The only egress this app actually makes is:
• Convex  — realtime sync (wss), queries/mutations and file storage
on <deployment>.convex.cloud, HTTP actions on .convex.site.
WILDCARDED on purpose: prod, dev and every Vercel preview
use a DIFFERENT deployment subdomain, so pinning one host
would break previews.
• 0.peerjs.com — the default PeerJS cloud signalling server (`new Peer()`
with no options). Only reached on the multiplayer path.
• dl.polyhaven.org — per-map HDRI environment maps fetched at runtime by
utils/HDRIEnvironment.ts for image-based lighting (High/Ultra
tiers only; low tiers skip the load). REMOVING THIS BREAKS
scene lighting on those tiers. The long-term fix is to
self-host the .hdr files and drop this origin entirely.
• Vercel Analytics / Speed Insights — same-origin /_vercel/*, so 'self'.
WebRTC STUN/TURN is NOT governed by connect-src, so P2P media is unaffected.
img-src is likewise narrowed: auth is username/password with NO OAuth
provider, so no external avatar hosts exist. Player photos come from
Convex storage. UserAvatar already falls back on error.
'wasm-unsafe-eval' is load-bearing for Rapier — do not remove it.

//: Re-opens Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy for public media only. The global
rule sets same-origin, which is right for HTML and JS; but og-image.jpg,
the icons and the trailer are meant to be fetched by other origins
(social cards, feed readers, the webmanifest). Social scrapers fetch
server-side where CORP is not enforced, so this is belt-and-braces —
it just removes a whole class of 'why is my preview image blank'.
The static content pages are pure HTML: no JavaScript, no network calls,
no WASM, no third-party anything. So they get a far stricter CSP than the
game does — default-src 'none' with only what they actually use added back.
Two subtleties, both deliberate:
• script-src stays 'self' rather than 'none' ONLY so the
<script type="application/ld+json"> structured-data block is
unambiguously safe. It is a data block, not executable script, but the
whole point of these pages is that Google parses that JSON-LD, and it
is not worth gambling the site's structured data on spec nuance.
Nothing is exploitable here: an attacker would need to place a .js file
on this origin, which the static build makes impossible.
• manifest-src 'self' is REQUIRED — every page links /site.webmanifest,
and manifests fall back to default-src, so 'none' would block it.
media-src 'self' covers the trailer <video> on /trailer.
External <a href> links (GitHub) are navigations and are not CSP-governed.
